_about: Synthetic, not from any real ticket: a React/TypeScript web client (i18n JSON labels, an OIDC config) and a Python/FastAPI backend, to show the grounding re-read is not iOS-specific. The plan makes the same three mistakes SK-2719's did: a label in the ticket's wording, a rule restated from part of a function, and a backend case that reproduces the web app's call without the web app's token scopes.

files_changed.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
+
+router = APIRouter()
+
+@router.post("/refunds")
+async def create_refund(body: RefundRequest, user=Depends(require_scopes("refunds:write"))):
+    order = await orders.get(body.order_id)
+    if order is None:
+        raise HTTPException(404, "Order not found")
+    if order.status != "Delivered":
+        raise HTTPException(409, "Only delivered orders can be refunded")
+    return await refunds.create(order)

happy_path.title: Request a Refund is offered for a refundable order
happy_path.preconditions: Signed in to the web app as a shopper with a delivered order.
steps: Open Orders and open the order's actions menu.
happy_path.expected: The menu item is enabled only for orders whose status is 'Delivered' and that have not been refunded (refundedAt is null).

integration_tests.title: POST /refunds rejects an order that is not delivered
steps: Pick an order the web app shows as not refundable because it is still in transit.
POST {baseUrl}/refunds with {"order_id": <id>} and Authorization: Bearer <user token>.
integration_tests.expected: 409 with detail 'Only delivered orders can be refunded'.
